newsitem.title: USA: Johnson & Johnson to buy Biopsys Medical.
newsitem.headline: Johnson & Johnson to buy Biopsys Medical.

text.p: Johnson & Johnson said on Thursday it would acquire Biopsys Medical, a California producer of products for breast biopsies, in a stock swap valued at about $310 million.

Under the terms of deal, Biopsys shareholders would receive Johnson & Johnson stock worth $27.55 for each Biopsis share, slightly higher than the company's closing price of $25.75 Wednesday on Nasdaq. Johnson & Johnson closed Wednesday at $59.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
With the purchase, Johnson & Johnson will acquire Biopsys' products for diagnosing breast cancer using a "minimally invasive" procedure.

"This is a very important strategic advance for our worldwide minimally invasive surgery franchise," said William C. Weldon, Johnson & Johnson company group chairman. "While we are delighted with the agreement, we are even more excited about the potential this innovative technology has for improving the quality of life for women around the world."
The merger is subject to the approval of Biopsys Medical stockholders and other customary conditions, including clearance under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act.
The ratio for the share exchange will be determined based on the average price of Johnson & Johnson stock during a 20-day period prior to Biopsys' stockholders' approval of the deal.
